newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March weekly earnings rise 2.7 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada March weekly earnings rise 2.7 pct on year.

text.p: The preliminary estimate of average weekly earnings for Canadian workers in all industries except agriculture and fishing rose 2.7 percent in March from a year earlier to a seasonally adjusted C$594.68, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
From the month before, earnings fell 0.3 percent.
Seasonally adjusted payroll employment rose 0.2 percent or 18,000 employees in March to 11.18 million from 11.16 million in February.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast that average weekly earnings would rise by 3.6 percent, year-on-year, after a 3.6 percent rise in February.

Statistics Canada said its survey of weekly earnings and payrolls was in the final phase of a project to improve estimates. Since the agency is changing methodology, it said there is a risk the payroll estimates may show a different seasonal pattern than previous data and should be assessed over a long time period.

Last month Statistics Canada had to revise payroll employment numbers for January and December after discovering a significant error in processing for those months. Officials say the error has been corrected.
